title: A generator-containing maximal localization is analytically unramified
statement: Let $R$ be a normal Nagata domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] [def-weil-pbc-nagata-ring], let $K$ be its fraction field, and let $x\in K$. Put $S=R[x]\subseteq K$, and assume explicitly that $R$ and $S$ are Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $S$ containing $x$, the local domain $S_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is analytically unramified [def-weil-pbc-analytically-unramified]: its maximal-ideal-adic completion is reduced.

proof.text: If x=0 it is integral, so S=R[x] is finite over R. The finite-over-Nagata theorem and Nagata localization show that A=S_m is Nagata; the local-Nagata-domain theorem makes A analytically unramified.

If x is nonzero, injectivity of S into its prime localization makes t=x/1 nonzero, and the image of m is the local maximal ideal, so t belongs to it. The principal-quotient-conditions lemma supplies no embedded primes, regular associated-prime localizations, and analytically unramified prime quotients. Apply the principal-quotient criterion.
